title: Hot and Cold: hideg, hűvös, meleg, forró

sections.title: From cold to scorching
sections.content: Hungarian has four everyday temperature words that step from cold to hot: hideg ("cold"), hűvös ("cool"), meleg ("warm/hot") and forró ("scorching hot", almost always for things you could burn yourself on: forró leves, forró nyár). Use them the same way as the other weather words, with van: Hideg van. Hűvös van. Meleg van. To ask the exact number, use fok ("degree"): Hány fok van? ("How many degrees is it?")

items.spanish: Ma nagyon hideg van, csak öt fok.
items.english: It's very cold today, only five degrees.

items.spanish: Hűvös van reggel, de délután meleg.
items.english: It's cool in the morning, but warm in the afternoon.

items.spanish: Nyáron néha 35 fok is van, forró a levegő.
items.english: In summer it's sometimes even 35 degrees, the air is scorching.

sections.content: forró is stronger than meleg — use it for things that are uncomfortably or dangerously hot (forró kávé, "hot/scalding coffee"), not just a pleasantly warm day.
